messages.content: Approval came through for the open-jaw plan. Can we move this from holds into actual reservations? I need SLC to Minneapolis on Sunday Nov. 10 after about 1 PM, then Milwaukee to SLC Thursday Nov. 14 after the 10:45 meeting. One connection is fine if it is not stressful. Also please request window seats where you can, reserve a car with room for materials boxes, and lock the three hotels with queen beds, breakfast, parking details, and dinner nearby.

Yes. The one piece I want you to choose is the Thursday return because it affects connection comfort. Outbound is easy: Delta nonstop SLC-MSP, 2:20 PM to 5:58 PM, $281. Return choices: Delta via Detroit, 3:05 PM to 7:40 PM, 1h42 connection, $386; United via Denver, 2:15 PM to 6:25 PM, 1h10 connection, $319; Delta via Minneapolis, 12:25 PM to 4:45 PM, 42-minute connection, $332. I would skip the 42-minute one. Do you want the cheaper United routing or the Delta routing with the bigger cushion?
Do the Delta via Detroit. The extra cost is easier to justify than sprinting through a connection.

Flight is set as Delta SLC-MSP Sunday 2:20-5:58 nonstop, then MKE-DTW-SLC Thursday 3:05-7:40 with 1h42 in Detroit. Window seats selected or requested where the map allowed: 14A outbound, 18F MKE-DTW, and 21A DTW-SLC. Fare total is $667. For the car, the midsize SUV is $347 plus taxes, pickup MSP Sunday around 6:30 PM and drop MKE Thursday about 1:15 PM. A standard car is about $60 less but tight for boxes.
Reserve the SUV. What hotel set came out best? I would rather keep St. Paul both Sunday and Monday if it is not over cap.

Best practical set: St. Paul Sunday-Monday, Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown, $151/night, two-queen refundable room, breakfast from 6:00, parking $15/night, several dinner spots within a few blocks. Madison Tuesday, Hampton Madison East Towne, $139, queen room, breakfast from 6:00, free parking, chain restaurants and a grocery close by. Brookfield Wednesday, Fairfield Inn & Suites Milwaukee Brookfield, $156, two queens, breakfast from 6:30, free parking, restaurants along Bluemound Road. All three show queen bedding rather than double-only rooms.
Book those refundable. One queen is fine when available; two queens is fine if that is the refundable option. Please add a late-arrival note for Sunday.

Reserved. St. Paul confirmation ends 4821, Madison 7736, Brookfield 9154. Notes added: late arrival Sunday after MSP flight, please hold confirmed queen-bed room type, traveler arriving with admissions materials. Breakfast hours and parking were confirmed from the hotel listings today; I would still glance at the front desk signs on arrival in case of holiday-week staffing changes. Cancellation windows are Saturday for St. Paul, Monday evening for Madison, and Tuesday evening for Brookfield.
Can you give me the reimbursement note, especially for the higher airfare and one-way car?

Use this: Recommended routing is SLC-MSP outbound and MKE-SLC return because the recruitment path moves east across Minnesota and Wisconsin and ends in the Milwaukee area. Although the open-jaw airfare and one-way SUV rental are modestly higher than a Minneapolis round trip, they avoid a Thursday backtrack of several hours, reduce winter-driving risk, and keep the traveler available for the 10:45 Milwaukee meeting. The midsize SUV is needed to transport admissions materials securely between school visits and fairs.
Great. Anything else before I put the receipts into Concur?

Upload the flight receipt, rental estimate, and all three hotel confirmations. Add the St. Paul parking line separately so it does not look like an unexplained rate increase. For materials, keep the box label list on your phone, bring the folio bag inside each night, and leave nothing visible in the car. I also added reminders for hotel cancellation deadlines, flight check-in, and a Thursday airport departure target of 12:45 PM from the Milwaukee stop.

messages.content: Delta just changed my Milwaukee return. The Detroit connection is now 39 minutes, which feels too tight. Also the forecast for Tuesday and Wednesday looks like early winter slush, the Madison hotel says breakfast will start at 6:30 instead of 6, and Milwaukee sent a separate materials drop-off gate for Thursday. Can you help me clean this up?

I would not keep the 39-minute Detroit connection unless arriving early is more important than reliability. Options now: keep it and land around 7:30 if everything works; move to Delta via MSP, 4:20 PM to 9:35 PM with a 1h18 connection, about $42 more or possibly covered by the schedule-change waiver; or switch to United via Denver, 2:55 PM to 7:10 PM with only 55 minutes. My vote is the later Delta via MSP if getting home around 10:15 is acceptable.
Move me to the later Delta. Late is better than sprinting or missing it.

Changed to MKE-MSP-SLC, departing 4:20 PM and arriving SLC 9:35 PM. Window seats were reselected/requested on both legs. I moved the rental return target to 2:45 PM, which gives you time for the Thursday drop-off gate, receipt check, and security. Build in 30 extra minutes Tuesday from St. Paul toward western Wisconsin and 45 extra minutes Wednesday into Madison if slush actually develops.
For Madison, I have a 7:15 visit in Sun Prairie and need to leave by 6:20. What is the breakfast plan?

Do not rely on the hotel breakfast that morning. On Tuesday night, grab yogurt, fruit, and a protein bar from the nearby grocery or Kwik Trip and keep it in the room fridge. Use lobby coffee if it is out early; otherwise get coffee after the school visit. Panera opening at 6 is too tight with weather.
Can you give me a tight packing and receipt checklist? I leave Sunday.

Checklist: printed schedule plus host phone numbers; Delta change email and new boarding passes; rental agreement and fuel receipt; hotel folios with parking separated; campus parking or gate instructions for Milwaukee; materials inventory photo before pickup and before return; one snow brush or scraper from home; boots or shoes that can handle slush; phone charger in the car; all receipts photographed nightly. Do not leave counselor cards, scanner, or folio bag in the SUV overnight.

messages.content: The recruiting trip is finally wrapped, so now I need to face Thanksgiving. My spouse's family confirmed San Diego. We can leave after early school release Wednesday Nov. 27 and need to be back Sunday Dec. 1 at a sane hour for Monday school and work. Four of us. Relatives have very limited sleeping space, so probably a hotel. Can you compare flying versus driving?

I can. For that holiday window, flying will protect Monday better, but driving may be much cheaper if fares have jumped. I need the relatives' neighborhood and the earliest realistic airport departure. Also, should I assume all four travel together, or do you want me to price a split plan with only part of the family going?
All four if we can make it work. They are near Clairemont Mesa Boulevard and I-5. We could leave the house around 1 PM Wednesday. If airfare is awful, driving is still on the table.

Here is the practical comparison. Fly all four: Southwest nonstop SLC-SAN 5:20-6:25 Wednesday and SAN-SLC 3:05-5:55 Sunday, about $408 per person or $1,632 total; Delta nonstop 3:45-4:50 Wednesday and 6:15-9:10 Sunday, about $462 per person or $1,848 total; cheapest late combo is about $1,504 total but lands close to midnight Sunday. Drive: about 750 miles each way, 11-12 hours without much margin; direct Wednesday after school gets you in very late, and splitting through Las Vegas adds motel cost and cuts into Thanksgiving morning. Hotel areas: Kearny Mesa/Clairemont is closest, Mission Valley has more food, Old Town is workable but parking is often pricier.
If we can keep airfare under about $1,700, I would rather fly. The Southwest timing looks best. For the hotel, two queens, breakfast, parking, and easy food would help.

One trade-off: Southwest saves money and includes bags, but seats are not assigned. For four people on a holiday flight, I would set check-in alarms or add EarlyBird if the price is reasonable. Delta costs about $216 more total on the current fares and lets you choose seats now. Is the savings worth the open seating for this trip?
For this one, yes. The teenagers can handle not sitting right next to us. Let's do Southwest and set check-in alarms.

Then I would hold the Hampton Inn San Diego-Kearny Mesa. It is closest to the Clairemont/I-5 area, about $189/night refundable, two-queen room available, breakfast starts at 6:00, free parking, and there are casual restaurants on Convoy and Clairemont Mesa nearby. Backups: Holiday Inn Express Mission Bay at about $204 with breakfast but some parking uncertainty, or Homewood Suites Mission Valley around $229 with more space but higher parking and a longer drive to relatives.
Hold the Hampton. Relatives can pick us up Wednesday, but not Sunday, so rideshare back to the airport is fine. Please make sure the Sunday return does not wreck Monday.

Held: Southwest outbound Wednesday 5:20 PM SLC to 6:25 PM SAN, return Sunday 3:05 PM SAN to 5:55 PM SLC. That return is the best balance I found because it avoids the late-night holiday crowd and gets everyone home before dinner. Hampton Kearny Mesa is held Wednesday through Sunday in a two-queen refundable room. Add a rideshare budget of about $35-$50 for the Sunday hotel-to-airport trip depending traffic.
Can you send me a quick family-thread summary with the budget?

Send this: Thanksgiving plan is to fly all four of us to San Diego instead of doing the 11-12 hour drive each way. Southwest nonstop leaves SLC Wednesday at 5:20 PM and returns Sunday at 3:05 PM, landing around 5:55 PM so Monday is protected. Airfare is about $1,632 total. Hotel hold is Hampton Inn San Diego-Kearny Mesa, two queens, breakfast included, free parking, close to Clairemont/I-5 and nearby casual food, about $756 before taxes for four nights. We will set Southwest check-in alarms and use rideshare to the airport Sunday.
